questions.q:
A graphic designer has developed a new range of birthday cards.

Which combination of factors is most likely to determine the success of the designs?
questions.explanation: Birthday cards are inexpensive, visually-driven products, so their success depends mainly on their appearance (aesthetics) and price (cost). Durability and technical function are not significant factors for a card that is used briefly.

questions.q: Which method would be the most effective to determine the target market of a consumer product?
options: Employ an entrepreneur to evaluate the product
Gather a focus group to complete a questionnaire about the product
Post a comment about the product on social media and ask for responses
Take a prototype of the product to the local shopping centre and ask shoppers for their opinions
questions.explanation: A focus group completing a questionnaire gathers structured, comparable data from a selected sample of potential users, making it the most reliable way to identify the target market. Social media comments and casual shopper opinions are unstructured and unrepresentative.

questions.q: At which part of the design process would a designer know that a product is viable?
questions.explanation: Researching products already on the market lets the designer gauge demand and feasibility, confirming whether a comparable product is commercially viable before committing time and resources. Production and idea generation occur after viability has been established.

questions.q:
An innovative gardening tool which helps the elderly plant seeds has been designed. The designer has developed some initial drawings and sketches and has created a company to produce the tool.

What will the designer need to do to protect the initial ideas?
questions.explanation: A patent protects a new, inventive functional device such as the gardening tool, giving the designer exclusive rights to the idea. Trademarks protect names, registering a business does not protect the design, and Standards Australia sets standards rather than protecting IP.

questions.q: Which of the following best outlines why designers would use 3D modelling when presenting their designs to manufacturers?
options: To ensure that the design is aesthetically appealing
To clarify any issues that may occur during production
To allow the manufacturers to visualise the final design
To show the manufacturers what the product must achieve
questions.explanation: A 3D model gives manufacturers a realistic, three-dimensional visualisation of the finished product, communicating form and detail more clearly than a 2D drawing. The other options are purposes served by briefs, prototypes or evaluation rather than the presentation model.

questions.q:
A design team is about to start developing a new range of products. Part of this process is the implementation of management plans.

These plans ensure that the products
options: are developed on time and on budget.
meet the needs of the target market.
questions.explanation: Management plans — action, time and finance plans — sequence tasks and allocate resources so the product is delivered on schedule and within budget. Meeting purpose, legal needs and the target market are achieved through other parts of the design process.

questions.q: Which of the following best outlines why designers undertake research and experimentation when developing a product?
options: To determine the properties of the materials to be used
To ensure all the materials are available for production
To ensure the best tools, materials and techniques are used
questions.explanation: Research and experimentation let the designer test options and select the most appropriate tools, materials and techniques for the product. Determining material properties is only one part of this broader aim.

questions.q:
A designer wants to create a new computer game and has established the design brief.

What will be included in the next step?
options: Looking at similar products on the market
Identifying the limitations and doing working drawings
questions.explanation: Once the brief is established the next step is research — examining similar products already on the market to understand what exists and what is needed. Sketches, working drawings and prototypes follow later in the process.

questions.q:
Many new homes are designed with ‘open plan’ living spaces.

What is likely to have most influenced this design?
questions.explanation: Open-plan living reflects changing social trends in how families want to live, relax and interact together at home. It is driven by lifestyle preferences rather than by technology, culture or household numbers.

questions.topic: Factors affecting design, success of innovation
questions.q: Which combination of factors is the most important for a designer to consider when developing a new app?
questions.explanation: In a fast-moving software market, the success of a new app depends most on the marketing strategy and the timing of its release so it reaches users ahead of competitors. The other factors are relevant but secondary to getting the product to market effectively.

questions.q:
Offices are changing and many now include work stations like those shown in Figures 1–4 (a range of ergonomic workstations, including a reclined support frame, adjustable polymer connectors, a stand-up workstation and a sit-to-stand desk).

(a) Outline a different ergonomic benefit in each of the workstations shown in Figure 1 and Figure 4. (2 marks)

(b) How have technological changes influenced the design of workstations such as those shown? (3 marks)

criteria.descriptor: (a) Sketches in general terms the ergonomic benefits of the workstations shown in Figure 1 and Figure 4
(b) Clearly demonstrates technological changes that have influenced the design of workstations like those shown
(b) Sketches in general terms how technological changes have influenced the design of workstations like those shown

questions.modelAnswer: (a) In Figure 4 the worker can move between sitting and standing while working, relieving the stress of staying in one position for long periods. Figure 1 shows the worker reclined in a frame, letting gravity act on the body at a different angle and relieving the stress that builds in a normal upright posture. (b) Improved materials and processing techniques have shaped these workstations — the wider use of new and existing polymers allows easy, accurate manufacture of components such as adjustable connectors, while smaller, lighter modern computers mean a stand-up workstation can be moved around the workplace safely, which would not have been possible with larger, heavier equipment.

questions.q: Describe the difference between designing a brand new product and redesigning a product that already exists.

criteria.descriptor: Describes the difference between designing a new product and redesigning one that already exists
Outlines the difference between designing a new product and redesigning one that already exists
Identifies some aspect of designing a new product and/or redesigning one that already exists

questions.modelAnswer: When redesigning an existing product, the designer can examine the current product and carry out market research — for example a PMI analysis or consumer surveys — to gauge responses to its function, features and appearance, then use those insights to improve it. Designing a brand new product relies far more on research and development of concepts and prototypes; this is more costly and time-consuming and can delay the product's release, but it is necessary because there is no existing product to learn from.

questions.q: Explain how the use of new and emerging technologies has had negative effects on the security for the individual in the workplace.

criteria.descriptor: Makes evident the relationship between the use of new and emerging technologies and negative effects on security for an individual in the workplace
Shows some relationship between the use of new and emerging technologies and negative effects on security for an individual in the workplace
Describes new and emerging technologies and their effects on security for an individual
Sketches in general terms new and emerging technologies and/or security for an individual

questions.modelAnswer: Biometric security technologies can lock the genuine user out: fingerprint recognition fails when grit, moisture or grease make the scan unreadable, and face recognition fails if the employee's appearance changes — growing a beard, wearing sunglasses or suffering a facial injury. Identification cards deny access when an employee forgets or loses them, and PINs (often four digits used with a swipe card in a two-tier system) can be systematically worked out once someone has the card, while passwords and PINs are easily forgotten. In each case the very technology meant to improve security can instead reduce the individual's reliable, secure access in the workplace.

questions.q:
Analyse how new and emerging technologies have improved current communication methods.

Your answer will be assessed on how well you: demonstrate knowledge and understanding relevant to the question; communicate ideas and information using relevant examples; and present a logical and cohesive response.

criteria.descriptor: Shows a comprehensive understanding of how new and emerging technologies have improved communication methods; draws out and relates these improvements to technologies; provides a logical and cohesive response, supported by relevant examples
Explains how new and emerging technologies have improved communication methods; communicates using relevant examples; provides a mostly logical and cohesive response, supported by relevant examples
Describes how new and emerging technologies have improved communication methods; provides a mostly organised response, supported by relevant example(s)
Outlines new and emerging technologies and/or improvements to communication methods; provides example(s)
Demonstrates some understanding of new and emerging technologies and/or communication methods

questions.modelAnswer: New and emerging technologies have made communication faster, more convenient and more personal. Voice recognition software records and transmits data as text across networks, adding speed and convenience. Real-time video messaging such as FaceTime enables instant 'face-to-face' communication over vast distances and can record images and video, making contact both immediate and personal. Email over computer networks disseminates information efficiently to one or many in a quick, convenient and inexpensive way, while social media such as Facebook and Snapchat allow instant communication between connected parties. Cloud storage lets documents be stored and retrieved anywhere via internet or mobile networks, giving flexibility in the workplace, and wearable technologies such as the Apple Watch let people communicate independently of a connected mobile phone. Together these technologies show a clear improvement in the speed, reach, flexibility and richness of modern communication methods.
